name: Ingrid Solberg
action: Ingrid presses the clipboard to her chest for a second, then sets it down on the table, her hand still resting on its edge. She glances at the three trays, then at the windowsill where the engine bolt sits, before speaking in her clipped coastal dialect: 'Three trays not yet brined, crew short one tonight. Supplier sent a half-percent off—I have to re-check everything myself. I can't leave this.' Her voice softens, almost reluctantly: 'But I can see the light from here. It's like that July evening. We'll go out tomorrow night, once the batch is smoked. I'll set the timer.'
reason: The engine hum and the memory of the July sunset with Kjersti pulled at Ingrid, but the residual worry over the supplier’s half-percent deviation, the three trays awaiting brine, and the short-staffed night crew triggered her established tendency to stay whenever a batch is at risk. Judging this batch to be at risk, she concluded she could not leave, yet because Kjersti had waited six years, she could not simply refuse either. So she gave an honest account of the batch’s needs and softened her refusal with a promise to go out tomorrow night if the smokehouse schedule allowed, and with a commitment to set a timer.
